# Dataset, Group 15

## synthetic/ (generated by `synthetic/generate.py`, `make_synthetic(T=3000, n, seed)`)
Files shipped: `synthetic_n3_seed{0,1,2}.csv` and `synthetic_n{5,9}_seed0.csv`, 3,000 days each. The other four (n = 5 and 9, seeds 1 and 2) were left out to fit the upload size limit; they regenerate identically with `python experiments/regen_synthetic.py --n 9 --seed 1 --out synthetic_n9_seed1.csv` (checked equal to the original files).
Columns: `day`; `regime` (hidden truth, 0 calm, 1 stress); `ret_i` (continuous return of asset i); `sym_i` (symbol 0/1/2 = down/ordinary/up, equal-probability cut points of a standard normal).
Process: two-state Markov chain (stay 0.98 calm, 0.95 stress). Calm: volatility 1.0, correlation 0.2, no drift. Stress: volatility 2.5, correlation 0.6, drift -0.3. Return = shared market shock + asset-specific shock; all assets are treated alike.
Use: every model is first tested on this data because the true regime is known (Section 5.2 of the paper).

## real/ (Yahoo Finance via yfinance, adjusted close, 1 Jan 1999 to 30 Sep 2026)
Basket A, US sector ETFs: XLB, XLE, XLF, XLI, XLK, XLP, XLU, XLV, XLY.
Basket B, developed-country ETFs: EWA, EWC, EWG, EWH, EWJ, EWP, EWQ, EWS, EWU.
Cleaning: forward-fill gaps of at most one day; keep days where all assets trade (the gap logs show no fills or trims were needed).
Size: 6,977 trading days (4 Jan 1999 to 29 Sep 2026) x 9 assets per basket.
Files: `basketA_us_sectors_adj_close.csv`, `basketA_us_sectors_log_returns.csv`, `basketB_developed_countries_adj_close.csv`, `basketB_developed_countries_log_returns.csv` (log returns = ln(P_t / P_{t-1}), first day dropped, so 6,976 rows).
`processed/`: `us_sectors.npz` and `developed_countries.npz` (the arrays the models read: dates, assets, returns, std_returns, rolling corr; 6,913 days from 7 Apr 1999 after the 64-day feature warm-up; returns match the log-return CSVs) and the two `*_gaplog.json` cleaning logs.
SPY and VIX context series are not included; they are only used for plots and the VIX variant of R2, never as model inputs.
Use: walk-forward folds (expanding window from 2005, six-month test blocks); regime labels R1 to R4 are built from these series and used only for scoring (Section 4.8 of the paper).

Note: the two processed `.npz` files (us_sectors.npz, developed_countries.npz, about 3.4 MB each) are left out of this copy to keep the file small; the gap logs are kept. They are in the full G15_Submission.zip and are rebuilt from the price CSVs by the repo's data pipeline.
